meta.title: Where Is the Sun?
meta.textType: story: a poem with repeated words

paragraphs: On Tuesday morning, there is a white fog. It is a quiet, foggy morning. A storm came last night, and the road is still wet. It is pet day at school, so Tom walks Lily and Pip there. "I can't see the road," says Tom. "There is not enough light." He holds Lily's hand, so she can stay close. Their shoes make a soft sound on the road. Lily whispers, "Where is the sun?" "Where is the sun?" Tom whistles, and Pip runs to the gate.

The fog stays on the road all the way to school. At school, Teacher Kim's class writes a poem about the fog. "Every verse needs a line that comes back," says Teacher Kim. "We can use my line," says Lily. The class writes the first verse on the board. "Where is the sun? Where is the sun?" "Fog, fog, go away!" "The sun will come, the sun will come."

Then the children write a second verse. "Where is the sun? Where is the sun?" "The fog is low, and the sky is high." "The sun will come, the sun will come." Teacher Kim reads all of the poem out loud. The class says the same line with her, again and again. The children like the sound of the words. They look out of the window, but the fog is still there.

By lunch, the fog goes away. The sun is high, and the school field is warm. The children sit on the grass with their lunch. They eat and talk about the poem. Pip lies still in the sun near the gate. "The sun came," says Lily. "What a wonderful day!" says Teacher Kim.
text.summary: On a foggy morning, Lily whispers a line about the sun. Her class writes a poem with the line in each verse, and the sun comes out.
